csa_63rd_tn_service.title: Compiled service record, Pvt. Hiram Sams, Co. F, 63rd Tennessee Infantry, CSA
csa_63rd_tn_service.repository: U.S., Confederate Soldiers Compiled Service Records, 1861-1865 (Ancestry, collection 2322, record 79171986); U.S., Civil War Soldier Records and Profiles, 1861-1865 (Ancestry, collection 1555, record 3223744)
csa_63rd_tn_service.note: Image read here (derived/compiled index cards, not a single scanned document; the underlying jacket is on Fold3 only). One card gives rank "Fifer", age 30, birth year abt 1832, enlisted 14 May 1862 at Sullivan Co., Tennessee (i.e. Zollicoffer), unit "Sixty-Third Infantry (Fain's Regiment, Seventy-Fourth Infantry)". A second, separately compiled profile gives enlistment/muster 30 Jul 1862, rank Private, Company F, 63rd Infantry — the two enlistment dates conflict slightly, ordinary for cards compiled from different muster rolls. Neither card shown carries the AWOL/desertion dates; those come from prior_ai_research's earlier pass over the fuller service jacket. Enrolled 14 May 1862 at Zollicoffer. Absent without leave from 1 June 1863; formally declared a deserter 1 April 1864. No record of him survives after that date.

marriage_1886_smith_hall.title: Marriage, William Smith & Jennie Hall, 26 Jun 1886
marriage_1886_smith_hall.note: Image read here (Washington County Court, Marriage Register H-Z 1785-1902; also indexed in "Virginia, Vital Records, 1715-1912" — the equivalent entry in "Virginia, Bureau of Vital Statistics, County Marriage Registers, 1853-1935" is affiliate-library restricted). William Smith, 21, b. c.1865, married Jennie Hall, 21. Parents indexed as "Sallie Smith" and "and[rew] Smith", confirming this is Andrew and Sallie's son William. Both parties are recorded as white — a contrast to William being recorded as Black in the 1870 and 1900 censuses. Taken at face value this looks like a different man; taken alongside this region's documented pattern of inconsistent racial recording for mixed-ancestry families (see Alice Louise Stovall's page), and a family photograph of Alice presenting as white, it may instead be the same man recorded differently in different contexts. Unresolved — his 1880 census entry (census_1880_smith) has not yet been pulled to give a third data point.

ancestry_tree_stovall_patrick_co.title: "Bartholomew Stovall Family Tree" profile for a John Quincy Alexander Stovall, b. Feb 1839 – d. 9 Jan 1929
ancestry_tree_stovall_patrick_co.note: Checked while looking for records of J. Q. A. Stovall's post-1878 life. This profile carries the same birth year (1839) and exact death date (9 Jan 1929) as our man, but its parentage and marriage conflict outright: birthplace Stuart, Patrick Co., VA (not Wilkes Co., N.C.); parents Archelaus Hughes Stovall & Mary Tabb Sandifer (not James & Ann Stovall per wash_co_va_marriage_1863); a wife Rebecca Williams (1847–1901) with five children born 1869–1879, then a later wife Frances C. Franklin — Mary E. Lester does not appear anywhere on this profile, and the child-bearing years overlap the period our man was still married to Mary. That part is read as a different, same-named Stovall (probably a cousin from the same southwest Virginia/NC border cluster) mistakenly merged into one profile. Its attached Confederate service record, however, checks out independently — see csa_51st_va_stovall, whose residence field (Glade Spring, Washington Co., VA) ties it to our man rather than the Patrick Co. one.

csa_51st_va_stovall.title: Confederate service record, Pvt. Quincy A. Stovall, Co. D, 51st Virginia Infantry
csa_51st_va_stovall.repository: U.S., Civil War Soldier Records and Profiles, 1861-1865 (Ancestry, collection 1555, record 1639537)
csa_51st_va_stovall.note: Image read here (a derived/compiled profile, not a single scanned document). Enlisted as a Private 14 Jun 1861 at Elamsville, Virginia; mustered into Co. D, 51st Virginia Infantry. Captured/imprisoned 16 Jul 1864 in "London County" [Loudoun Co.], Virginia — the same capture the outside Ancestry tree's POW card describes (received at Elmira, N.Y., 25 Jul 1864 from Old Capitol Prison, released 29 May 1865). Survived the war. Described as florid complexion, blue eyes, auburn hair, 5 ft. 8 in. Residence given as Glade Spring, Washington Co., Virginia — the decisive detail tying this service record to our man rather than to the Patrick Co. Stovall in ancestry_tree_stovall_patrick_co. Fits the timeline cleanly: enlisted 1861, married Mary E. Lester in Sept 1863 (presumably on furlough or between postings), captured Jul 1864, held as a POW until the war's end, then presumably returned home before leaving the family c.1878–80.

wash_co_va_marriage_1882.title: Marriage register, George W. Lewis & Harriet Eliza Sams, 1882
wash_co_va_marriage_1882.note: NOT LOCATED, despite an exhaustive search: the entire 1882 Washington Co. VA register paged by hand on Ancestry, plus FamilySearch's Historical Records (multiple surname spellings), Family Tree, Genealogies and full-text search. The only similarly-named entry is a different couple — "George H Lewis" (21, parents Samuel & Margaret Lewis) marrying "Harriet P. Salmons" (22) on 23 Oct 1882, recorded "colored" — confirmed by direct image read to be a different family on name, age, parents and race. The marriage itself is well corroborated independently (1900 census gives "Marriage Year 1882" for this household; Walter A. Lewis's 1955 TN death certificate names both parents), so it happened, but no register entry for it has been found in any searched collection. It may never have been formally returned to the county clerk.

delayed_birth_bettie_lewis_1949.note: Image read here. Bettie Jane Lewis, born 25 Sept 1896, Washington Co., VA. Father George W. Lewis, age 36 at her birth, Washington Co. VA. Line 11, "Mother of Child, full maiden name," reads "Harriett Booher", age 37 at the birth. Sworn statement by Mrs. Flora Mae Greever (relationship: sister-in-law), witnessed by notary David A. bible_notes_lewis.title: Handwritten notes on an old Lewis family Bible
bible_notes_lewis.note: Loose pages photographed here, of unknown authorship and date, mixing transcription of a Bible said to date to 1872 with later family recollection. Some entries are second- or third-hand. Separate notes found among the papers of Colleen Hoffman (Lorene Lewis's daughter) indicate that George W. Lewis himself wrote several of the entries in the underlying Bible; which of the transcribed lines are his is not marked. Records "Harriet Boar was in Old Bible" and that "Harret Bohr" is the form seen "more often in outside records"; also carries the Ike Ingram / housemaid story and a "Cherokee or Creek" ancestry note. A separate summary page gives George Lewis's parents as "William W.S. (Samuel William)" and "Elizabeth" with the family arriving from Charleston, SC in 1865 — contradicted outright by census and marriage records. Treated as highly questionable throughout.

census_1880_booher.title: 1880 U.S. census, Kinderhook District, Washington Co., Virginia — Jane Booher household
census_1880_booher.note: Image read here. Corrects an earlier index-only read: Jane Booher is herself the head of the household, not a step-mother in someone else's. Dwelling/family 675, Kinderhook District: Jane Booher, 40, white, widowed, keeping house, b. Tennessee, both parents b. Tennessee, cannot read or write; Jacob H. Booher, 19, stepson, farm laborer, b. Virginia — meaning Jane had already married and lost a first Mr. Booher by 1880; Elizabeth Samms, 16, daughter, at home, b. Tennessee — a younger Sams daughter (b. c.1863–1864), not Harriet. A different, apparently unrelated Booher family (James L. Booher, wife Rebecca, and their children) lives next door on the same page — see wash_co_va_marriage_1889_booher, where Jane goes on to marry this James L. Booher nine years later.

wash_co_va_marriage_1889_booher.title: Marriage record, James L. Booher & Jane Booher, 3 Apr 1889
wash_co_va_marriage_1889_booher.repository: Virginia, U.S., Marriage Registers, 1853-1935 (Ancestry, from the Library of Virginia)
wash_co_va_marriage_1889_booher.note: Image read here. Washington Co. VA register: James L. Booher, 56, and Jane Booher, 47, both white and both widowed, both giving residence "Washington Co." for the groom and "Sullivan Co., Tenn." for the bride — the same Tennessee county as Hiram Sams's own enlistment, corroborating this is the same Jane Carrier/Sams/Booher throughout. Ceremony performed by H. P. Waugh. James L. Booher is the same man recorded as a widower with grown children (Rebecca having died between the 1880 census and this marriage) two households away from Jane's own in the 1880 census — see census_1880_booher. This is Jane's third marriage on record (Hiram Sams, an unnamed first Mr. Booher by whom she was already widowed in 1880, then James L. Booher here), not documented anywhere before this search.

census_1880_ingram.title: 1880 U.S. census, Holston District, Washington Co., Virginia — I. H. Ingram household
census_1880_ingram.note: FamilySearch index consulted here. I. H. Ingram, merchant, born c.1852; household is a wife and two young daughters, no servants. Matches the initials, trade and locale of the "Ike Ingram" of the family's Bible notes, and he is buried at Friendship Cemetery as Harriet was — but no record places Harriet in his household.

census_1860_washington_lewis.title: 1860 U.S. census, Washington Co., Virginia — Philip Lewis household
census_1860_washington_lewis.note: Image read here. Western District, Washington Co., VA, enumerated 7 Aug 1860, p. 168, household #1201: Philip Lewis, 30, day labourer, personal estate $50, b. NC; wife Margaret, 24, housekeeper; daughter Virginia, 1. The family was already resident in Washington County five months before George's December 1860 birth — so there was no 1865 arrival from Charleston, SC, as the family Bible notes claim. Two households below (lines 23-29 are Elizabeth Owens' family; lines 30-31 are Philip Rouse's own household with wife Sarah; lines 32-40 are the separate household of Isaac Rouse, wife Margaret, and children) — Philip Rouse is very likely Margaret (Rouse) Lewis's birth family living next door, in his own household rather than folded into Isaac's.

va_births_1859_virginia_lewis.title: Birth register, Virginia E. Lewis, 17 Jul 1859
va_births_1859_virginia_lewis.repository: Virginia, Births and Christenings, 1584-1917 / Virginia, Vital Records, 1715-1912 (FamilySearch, from the Library of Virginia)
va_births_1859_virginia_lewis.note: Image read here (Register of Births, Upper District, Washington Co., VA, film 004023748, image 148). Virginia E Lewis, born 17 Jul 1859, Upper District, Washington Co., Virginia; father Philip Lewis, mother Margaret Lewis. The first primary record naming a Lewis daughter — Virginia — who does not appear anywhere in this project's earlier notes; she is also the "daughter Virginia, 1" of the following year's census (census_1860_washington_lewis).

census_1870_washington_lewis.title: 1870 U.S. census, Washington Co., Virginia — Margaret Lewis household
census_1870_washington_lewis.note: Image read here. Division 4, Washington Co., VA, enumerated 25 Oct 1870, p. 18, household #133: Margaret Lewis, 32, head of household (no husband recorded), b. Virginia; children Virginia (10), George (8), America (6), Missouri (3), all b. Virginia. Confirms Philip Lewis was already dead by this census — narrowing his death to before Oct 1870, rather than the fuller 1867–71 range previously carried on his own account — and gives primary-record backing, for the first time, to three daughters (Virginia, America, Missouri) previously known only from the family's Ancestry tree (see george_w_lewis's "His sisters" section). Virginia's age here (10) and the exact birth register (va_births_1859_virginia_lewis) agree to within a year, ordinary census rounding. CAVEAT (added after a 2026-09 image audit): the attached scan is a single page, and household #133 begins on its very last line (line 39, Margaret) with only Virginia's line (40) following before the page ends. George, America, and Missouri's ages/birthplaces are NOT actually visible on this image — they must appear on the following page (p. 19), which has not been captured here. Their inclusion in this household is well corroborated elsewhere (the family's own tree, and consistency with Margaret and Virginia's confirmed entries), but is not independently image-verified until that page is added.

lewis_death_cert_walter_1955.title: Death certificate, Walter Andrew Lewis, 8 Jan 1955
lewis_death_cert_walter_1955.repository: Tennessee, U.S., Death Records, 1908-1965 (Ancestry, from the Tennessee State Library and Archives)
lewis_death_cert_walter_1955.note: Image read here. Certificate #55-01026. Walter Andrew Lewis, white male, born 16 Oct 1883 in Virginia, died 8 Jan 1955 at Corryton, Knox Co., TN, age 71. Father George Lewis; mother "Harriet Sims" — an evident transcription variant of Sams. Cause of death sarcoma of the stomach. Informant Mrs. Grace Lewis, Corryton, TN. Buried East End Cemetery, Wytheville, VA.

numident_lewis_children.title: Social Security (NUMIDENT / SS-5) application, Walter A. Lewis
numident_lewis_children.repository: U.S., Social Security Applications and Claims Index, 1936-2007 (Ancestry)
numident_lewis_children.note: Image read here, but only for Walter: birth date 16 Oct 1883, birthplace Glade Spring, Virginia, claim date 14 May 1951, SSN 410-16-9505 — matching his 1955 death certificate exactly and confirming identity. This particular index entry does not display a mother's-maiden-name field, so it corroborates by birth date/place rather than itself stating "Sams"; the broader claim that several children's SS-5s give the mother's maiden name as Sams has not been re-verified for any sibling beyond Walter. James Hiram Lewis's entry in this collection gives an implausible "Washington Co., Pennsylvania" birthplace and was not treated as a confirmed match; no clean match was found for Frank T., Mary E. (Wyingear), Maggie (Freeman) or Betty (Barbra).
